source.title: Implementation of ResNet-50-Based Convolutional Neural Network For Mobile Skin Cancer Classification
source.authors: A. Asriani; Nouval Trezandy Lapatta; Deny Wiria Nugraha; A. Amriana; Wirdayanti Wirdayanti

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper. No material truncation or garbling affects the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests dropout and batch-size conditions in a new application setting: pretrained ResNet-50 skin-lesion classification. It reports test-set classification results and parameter-sweep accuracies, but does not test the claim’s central random-label memorization/generalization relationship.
record.gate_note: The study reports accuracy for ResNet-50 under data-split, dropout and batch-size conditions. It does not compare training and test error as a generalization gap, test random labels, or measure generalization properties such as sharpness. Results for MobileNet and InceptionV3 are comparisons of architectures, but the text does not give their training recipes or describe them as fully connected controls.
record.test_reason: The study uses dropout while tuning a skin-lesion classifier, but never compares dropout against no dropout or establishes excessive-dropout underfitting. Its batch-size sweep uses a 20-epoch maximum with early stopping, without establishing equal actual epoch budgets or a workload-dependent large-batch threshold. These tuning results do not test a listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: the selected pretrained ResNet-50 configuration uses a 70:30 split, dropout 0.4, batch size 64 and 20 epochs, achieving reported accuracy of 83.84% and weighted precision, recall and F1 of about 83%. They implemented it through a Flask API in an Android application as an early-detection aid requiring professional clinical diagnosis.
record.recipe_differences: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 with frozen initial layers, Adam, and task-specific classification layers; evaluates skin-lesion classification and dropout/batch-size settings rather than arbitrary-label memorization or the claim’s generalization-gap measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy changes across dropout, batch-size and training-data split combinations. The authors state that increasing dropout may decrease performance; their tables show the best configuration differs between 70% and 80% data splits.

fits_no_version.finding: Accuracy varies across nonzero dropout rates, batch sizes and data splits. At the 70% split and batch size 64, accuracy decreases from 83.84% to 82.37% to 81.05% as dropout increases; at the 80% split, the corresponding accuracies are 81.85%, 81.85% and 83.35%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this pretrained ResNet-50 skin-lesion classifier, preferred nonzero dropout settings depend on the data split and batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: Batch size 64 achieves the highest reported accuracy within every fixed dropout-and-split group among batches 16, 32 and 64. Actual training durations in epochs are not reported despite early stopping.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size 64 performs best among the tested batch sizes under this study's tuning procedure.

record.peer_reviewed: JOURNAL OF APPLIED INFORMATICS AND COMPUTING, Vol. 9, No. 4, August 2025
record.problems: No random-label or fully connected comparison; no matched no-dropout baseline; no training-error results sufficient to quantify the train-test gap. Parameter combinations were chosen by trial and error, and the text does not report uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: None. All 18 reported accuracy entries from Tables IV and V are included.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label training and held-out performance.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and effects of tuning or switching.
Large-batch penalties under verified fixed epoch budgets and recovery through recipe changes.
Benefit of adding dropout versus no dropout, very-small-training-set exceptions, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V6 limits_scope verdict: an untested no-dropout comparison is not evidence limiting the claim. The sweep does isolate differences between nonzero dropout rates when batch size and split are held fixed, contrary to several row notes, but those differences do not establish underfitting. Table III reports L2 regularization of 0.01. Figure 3 reports training accuracy reaching 100% and validation accuracy around 80%; this natural-label result alone does not test V1.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out performance relative to chance, and the same recipe’s behavior under both label conditions.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error behavior as width increases.
No fully connected image classifier comparison or test of local connectivity.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
No large-batch versus small-batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets; only a limited batch-size sweep is reported.

The text reports held-out accuracy under dropout settings, but does not test very small training sets, excessive-dropout underfitting as a distinct result, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
No perturbation-based sharpness or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples or comparison against random-example removal.

rows.size_stated: ResNet-50; model structure reports 23,587,712 parameters for the Resnet (Functional) component, plus classification layers
rows.operation_detail: Trained on HAM10000 with dropout 0.4 and batch size 64 under the 70% data split; 20 epochs with early-stopping callback
rows.locator: Table IV; Results and Discussion, A. Best Model
rows.note: The paper identifies this as the highest accuracy for the 70% data split. This is held-out classification accuracy, but the report does not establish the train-test gap.
rows.check: 83.84% is a selected configuration's accuracy, not evidence that dropout lowers error: no no-dropout baseline exists. Tables IV–V are described as validation-based configuration selection; this cell should not automatically be called independent test accuracy. The recipe also includes L2 regularization of 0.01.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CNN-ResNet50 on HAM10000 across the reported training-data splits and batch sizes
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports accuracies under dropout settings but has no matched no-dropout baseline, so it does not establish that dropout lowers held-out error; accuracies also vary across batch-size and split settings (R1–R18).
